definition: Reuse each newly collected physical transition for multiple gradient updates instead of discarding it after one policy update.
core_tradeoff: Higher update efficiency can reduce physical samples but increases sensitivity to replay distribution, reward quality and implementation latency.
failure_modes: critic divergence; stale replay; narrow task envelope; compute stalls; unsafe early exploration

definition: Learn a dynamics/performance surrogate from a small number of physical trials and optimize actions or policies through the surrogate.
core_tradeoff: Small physical trial counts are exchanged for model bias, planning/optimization compute and designed action spaces or costs.
failure_modes: model error under contact; optimizer exploitation; long compute between trials; narrow local validity

definition: Fit a compact predictive model during physical learning and improve behavior primarily through imagined rollouts or planning.
core_tradeoff: Hours of physical data may suffice, but reward engineering, representation error, model compute and task-specific resets remain.
failure_modes: model hallucination; compounding error; reward-model mismatch; contact dynamics underfit

definition: Pretrain or self-supervise visual features/goals so online RL does not learn perception and control entirely from sparse task reward.
core_tradeoff: Better representations reduce target-task samples but introduce pretraining data, augmentation choices and latent-reward bias.
failure_modes: representation ignores contact cues; latent distance misaligns with task success; transfer distribution shift

level3: Residual policy around an engineered controller
definition: Learn only a corrective residual on top of an existing controller rather than relearning the full policy.
core_tradeoff: Physical exploration shrinks, but controller design and optional simulator development become one-time costs.
failure_modes: base controller limits reachable behavior; residual overrides safety; transfer fails outside controller basin

definition: Train easier auxiliary behaviors and schedule them so sparse-reward target skills receive useful experience.
core_tradeoff: No demonstrations are needed, but auxiliary reward design and long physical training remain.
failure_modes: auxiliary tasks compete; scheduler neglects target; reward engineering dominates

definition: Exploit one-step task structure or data-efficient black-box search to learn from a bounded number of physical attempts.
core_tradeoff: Episode count can be small while physical cycle time, reset handling and between-trial optimization remain unmeasured.
failure_modes: trial-to-trial nonstationarity; poor state coverage; expensive physical cycle; no wall-clock accounting

definition: Run multiple comparable robots concurrently and aggregate their experience into one learner or dataset.
core_tradeoff: Calendar throughput improves, but aggregate robot-hours, capital, maintenance, object logistics and dataset curation increase.
failure_modes: fleet calibration drift; correlated failures; learner bottleneck; maintenance and staffing dominate

definition: Use another robot to lift, reposition or otherwise restore the learner so training continues without recurring direct handling.
core_tradeoff: Operator handling can fall, but a second robot, force sensing, calibration and coordination replace it.
failure_modes: teacher collision; synchronization failure; helper becomes task-specific fixture; capital cost exceeds saved labor

level3: Overlapped collection and learning on local accelerators
definition: Engineer the learner, replay, control and recovery path so policy updates occur during continued physical practice.
core_tradeoff: Wall-clock falls only if compute, control and reset do not block each other; hardware and software integration become material costs.
failure_modes: GPU/control contention; JIT/startup delay; stale policies; nondeterministic timing; logging bottleneck

definition: Learn or alternate behaviors whose terminal states furnish valid starts for another behavior.
core_tradeoff: Longer autonomous runs are possible, but task graphs, backward demonstrations and state coverage must be engineered.
failure_modes: both directions fail; state distribution drifts; object leaves reachable workspace; task graph has dead ends

definition: Choose goals or task phases so successful interaction naturally creates another training opportunity without restoring one canonical state.
core_tradeoff: Unattended duration improves, but the resulting state distribution may differ from the benchmark initial-state distribution.
failure_modes: object depletion; curriculum stalls; pseudo-reset hides state drift; battery or workspace limits

level3: Reset or recovery policy from demonstrations/data
definition: Train a controller that restores viable states after failure and interleave it with the forward policy.
core_tradeoff: Manual resets can be reduced after bootstrapping, but reset demonstrations and imperfect recovery create displaced labor and bias.
failure_modes: recovery outside demonstration support; reset policy traps; compounded forward/reset errors; unsafe retry

level3: Hand-coded reorientation, reels, gravity, launchers or actuated bins
definition: Use deterministic mechanisms or task fixtures to return the robot/environment to a viable state.
core_tradeoff: Reliable throughput is gained at the cost of task-specific engineering and limited portability.
failure_modes: fixture wear; unmodeled jam; recovery script cannot handle novel failure; benchmark over-instrumentation

level1: Shift learning out of the target online phase
level3: Offline pretraining then limited online fine-tuning
definition: Initialize a policy/value function from previously collected physical trajectories, then spend a smaller target-task online budget.
core_tradeoff: Marginal target interaction drops, but prior data collection, curation and distribution mismatch remain lifecycle costs.
failure_modes: extrapolation error; incompatible sensors/actions; negative transfer; hidden prior-data labor

level1: Shift learning out of the target online phase
definition: Train and evaluate the policy mainly from a fixed fleet-collected corpus rather than exploring online for the new run.
core_tradeoff: Deployment exploration risk falls, but the corpus can require tens of thousands of episodes and hundreds of robot/human hours.
failure_modes: dataset bias; missing recovery states; reward relabeling error; evaluation leakage; provenance loss

level1: Shift learning out of the target online phase
definition: Prepare a controller, residual initialization or behavior repertoire in simulation before bounded physical adaptation.
core_tradeoff: Physical adaptation can be short, but simulation compute, model construction and calibration are displaced costs.
failure_modes: sim-to-real mismatch; repertoire lacks needed behavior; adaptation destabilizes prior; compute bill unreported

level1: Shift learning out of the target online phase
level3: Full RL or policy improvement inside a learned video world
definition: Use a learned action-conditioned world as the main trial-and-error environment and reserve hardware for data acquisition or evaluation.
core_tradeoff: Robot interaction is replaced by pretrained data and accelerator time; imagined success may not transfer to contact-rich reality.
failure_modes: hallucinated dynamics; reward-model exploitation; coverage gaps; large GPU demand; evaluation-only physical evidence

definition: Seed replay, representations, policy behavior or world models with a small target-task demonstration set.
core_tradeoff: Unsafe random exploration is reduced, but demonstration collection time, expertise and coverage are rarely reported.
failure_modes: demonstration bias; insufficient failure coverage; embodiment mismatch; teleoperation latency; apparent sample efficiency hides labor

definition: Allow an operator to override or correct the learner online and train from those intervention transitions.
core_tradeoff: Training can converge in hours, but operator occupancy, expertise, fatigue and intervention quality become central costs.
failure_modes: late intervention; inconsistent operator policy; intervention distribution shift; hidden always-on monitoring

level3: Play, failure data and continuous multi-task collection
definition: Collect broad non-success-only interaction so the model/policy sees failures, contacts and diverse states.
core_tradeoff: Coverage improves, but collection volume and storage/curation cost can dominate target-task savings.
failure_modes: unsafe play; skew toward easy states; low-value repeated failures; detector bias; storage bottleneck

definition: Replace difficult instrumented rewards with learned classifiers or model-based progress judgments.
core_tradeoff: Reward instrumentation can be reduced, but label collection and reward-model error move into the lifecycle cost.
failure_modes: reward hacking; classifier drift; false success; domain shift; expensive label refresh

definition: Meta-train a dynamics model across conditions so a small amount of physical data adapts it to a new terrain or regime.
core_tradeoff: Fast adaptation inherits multi-condition physical meta-training and safety handling.
failure_modes: new condition outside meta-training support; unsafe adaptation data; model update instability

definition: Search a precomputed behavior map for a compensating controller after damage using a bounded number of physical tests.
core_tradeoff: Sub-two-minute physical adaptation depends on millions of simulated behaviors and does not represent from-scratch learning.
failure_modes: damage mode absent from repertoire; simulator bias; test damages hardware; map-generation compute hidden

definition: Adapt a pretrained policy while a teacher robot supplies recovery and safety actions.
core_tradeoff: Minute-scale adaptation is exchanged for teacher hardware, simulation pretraining and integration effort.
failure_modes: teacher/learner collision; force-sensor drift; adapted policy depends on tether or treadmill
